svg.title: Step 8 · Our own MCP server
svg.desc: Any MCP client posts to /api/mcp: one JSON-RPC message of at most 8 KiB, through our middleware. The official SDK's MCPServer keeps no session and answers in JSON. Its four tools are made from the same definitions the agent runs over REST: the input schema from the same model, the run within the same 8 s, through the same cache. Each answer carries the weather as structured content, the summary as text, and in _meta the request and whether the cache gave it; a failure, our sentence and its class.

Each answer
structuredContent: the weather · text: the summary · _meta: the request, fromCache · a failure: isError, our sentence, its class
Why no session: Vercel's copies share no memory, so a session begun on one would be unknown
on the next. Why returned, never raised: the SDK would write "Error executing tool" before our sentence.
Why public: it's the no-auth lane; step 11 limits how often one client may call it.
In the tests: the SDK's own client, in this process and over HTTP; the schemas agree; 413, 400, no CORS
One definition, two doors: the agent's REST tools, and an MCP server any client can call.
On serverless, MCP keeps no session, and answers in JSON.
